body:
Global crypto markets took a meaningful step back on October 22, with total market capitalization falling to $2.76T, a decline of -4.54% over the prior 24 hours on volume of $90.6B. The mood shifted decisively risk-off, driven by a confluence of AI sector doubt, an oil price surge, and weak equity signals out of Asia — with Tesla's Q3 results and a falling KOSPI adding to the pressure. Despite the selloff, the Fear and Greed index actually ticked higher, moving from 63 yesterday to 68 today, a reading that sits in Greed territory and suggests retail sentiment has not yet capitulated. BTC dominance held at 59.4%, with ETH dominance at 10.6%, and that divergence in relative strength tells you most of what you need to know about where money is sheltering today.

Bitcoin printed at $81,685 on 24-hour volume of $38.22B, down -2.19% on the day but still clinging to a positive weekly return of +0.93%. The headlines have it right: BTC slid below $82,000 during the session, a level that now flips to near-term resistance on any attempted recovery. The 1-hour decline of -0.30% suggests the selling pressure is not abating sharply into the close. The $80,000 handle is the next psychologically significant support, and a clean break below that on elevated volume would open the door to a more uncomfortable unwind. On the upside, reclaiming $82,000 with conviction is the minimum requirement before momentum traders re-engage. For now, BTC is the relative safe haven in the crypto complex, and that alone is telling you something about how the rest of the market looks.

ETH fell -2.71% to $2,400.86 on volume of $13.4B, fractionally underperforming BTC on a 24-hour basis but posting a slightly better 7-day return of +1.39%. The more interesting story is in the altcoin layer, where the damage was considerably worse. UNI was the hardest hit among ZIMR-tracked majors at -5.14%, landing at $7.10, consistent with the broader DeFi sector leading declines as noted in today's CoinDesk reporting. AVAX dropped -4.59% to $9.24, continuing a rough 7-day stretch of -3.17%. ADA fell -3.86% to $0.216495, also negative on the week at -2.25%, making it one of the cleaner expressions of broad altcoin underperformance. The relative outperformers — if you can call them that in a down tape — were BNB at -1.70% to $732.85, BTC, and XRP at -2.21% to $1.33. DOT and AVAX were the only assets showing positive 1-hour momentum at +0.75% and +0.17% respectively, though that's a thin reed in this environment.

The macro backdrop deteriorated on multiple fronts simultaneously. An AI selloff pulled risk appetite out of tech-adjacent assets globally, oil surged, and Asian equities weakened with the KOSPI notably down. Tesla's Q3 earnings appear to have acted as a sentiment trigger. In the regulatory lane, UK-focused commentary from Cointelegraph flagged continued friction around a workable path to regulated DeFi access, reinforcing that institutional onramps in major jurisdictions remain incomplete. Meanwhile, CoinDCX's pledge of no user losses following $16M in transfers drawing scrutiny adds a layer of exchange-level uncertainty, even if contained. ETF flows are described in today's CoinDesk reporting as wobbling, which matters because steady ETF inflows have been a pillar of BTC's bid in recent months — any sustained softness there removes a meaningful source of structural demand.

Looking ahead, the immediate catalyst to watch is whether BTC can defend $80,000 on a closing basis, because a breach there with volume would likely accelerate altcoin losses well beyond what we saw today. The AI narrative — both as a macro risk-off trigger and as a driver of on-chain sentiment around crypto-AI crossover projects — deserves close monitoring given it was cited as a direct headwind in multiple headline feeds. Ethereum's reported 4-minute settlement plan is worth tracking as a medium-term structural positive for ETH, but it will not move the needle in the current risk-off session. The Fear and Greed reading of 68 is a mild concern: the market is selling but sentiment has not reset to neutral, which historically leaves room for a deeper flush before a durable base forms. A recovery in equity markets, stabilization in oil, and a resumption of ETF inflows would need to arrive together to shift the picture back toward constructive.
